title: Tilt and Step Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Accelerometer
Tilt Detection
Step Counter
Thresholds
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim with a draggable 3D watch that shows the accelerometer's x, y and z readings and tilt rules, plus a simulated walk where students tune a step-count threshold and minimum time between steps.

educational.topic: Accelerometer tilt detection and step counting
learningObjectives: Apply the x, y and z readings of an accelerometer to decide whether a watch is face up or on a raised wrist
Analyze how the step threshold changes missed steps and extra steps
Explain why a minimum time between steps prevents one footstep from counting twice
prerequisites: Accelerometer basics and units of g

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Direct manipulation and parameter tuning against a known answer
keyQuestions: Why does the magnitude stay at 1 g when the watch is tilted?
What goes wrong when the threshold is too low or too high?
Why does a minimum time between steps fix double counting?
commonMisconceptions: An accelerometer at rest reads zero (it reads 1 g from gravity)
A lower threshold always catches more real steps (it also counts noise and second bumps)
assessmentOpportunities: Record axis readings for a tilt and check them against the chapter's rules
Find the threshold range where counted steps match real steps

controls.label: Walk / Stop
controls.description: Continues or pauses the simulated walk. Opens paused with 5 seconds already recorded.

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns the watch to flat and reloads the original recording, paused.
